name: dvisvgm
why: Turns TeX's DVI pages into SVG geometry, a neat transform, though TeX tooling is a niche corner.

brief.what_it_is: dvisvgm is a command-line utility for TeX and LaTeX users that converts DVI files into SVG, the XML-based vector graphics format. It also accepts EPS and PDF input through the --eps and --pdf options. The output is vector SVG, so it scales without loss of quality, unlike bitmap output. Fonts are handled by embedding glyph outlines, and the homepage says the SVG files display in modern browsers, Inkscape, and the Squiggle browser from Apache Batik.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage frames the tool as a way to get arbitrarily scalable vector graphics out of TeX documents, since bitmap graphics lose quality when scaled. It is aimed at TeX and LaTeX users who need SVG output.
brief.how_it_works: The converter reads DVI pages (classic version 2, pTeX vertical mode version 3, and XeTeX XDV versions 5, 6, and 7) and turns them into SVG geometry. It embeds glyph outlines for all required fonts, vectorizing METAFONT bitmaps on the fly when no vector font is available. It also evaluates many TeX specials (color, hyperref, papersize, PostScript and others) and uses preview-package bounding box data to report width, height, and depth so output can be baseline-aligned in HTML or XSL-FO.
brief.install_notes: The homepage names no install steps beyond the package managers it lists. dvisvgm is included in TeX Live, W32TEX, MiKTEX, and MacPorts. The README was not reached, so runtime requirements and first-run configuration are not known from these notes.
brief.standout: Rather than just rasterizing or wrapping TeX output, it reconstructs the page as SVG geometry and embeds the font outlines, with options to convert fonts to paths for renderers that lack SVG font support. It also uses preview-package depth data so inline graphics can sit on the text baseline.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage shows no release date, changelog, or last-updated note. It does say the tool ships in TeX Live, MiKTEX, W32TEX, and MacPorts, which suggests active packaging, but I could not confirm a recent release or commit.
brief.caveats: The homepage is the only page I could read. A guessed GitHub URL (github.com/mgieseking/dvisvgm) returned 404, so I could not check the README, the manual page, or any build instructions. The homepage refers to a manual page for the full option list but does not link it. The project is licensed GPL v3 or later. The homepage describes it as a niche TeX tool, and the scout note calls TeX tooling a niche corner.
quotes: The command-line utility dvisvgm is a tool for TEX/LaTEX users.
In contrast to bitmap graphics, vector graphics are arbitrarily scalable without loss of quality.
